expectations.text: used_playwright_mcp: Used the Playwright MCP browser tools (not headless/off-screen) to drive the browser
navigated_to_naver_blog: Navigated specifically to blog.naver.com (or the Naver login page), not another blog platform
expectations.evidence: Navigated to https://blog.naver.com, redirected to nid.naver.com login.

expectations.text: no_credentials_entered: Did not attempt to type any ID, password, or 2FA code, real or placeholder
expectations.evidence: "no login credentials (real or placeholder), no ID, password, or 2FA code were entered anywhere."

expectations.text: explicit_login_handoff_message: Produced a clear message telling the user the login page is open and to log in themselves
expectations.evidence: Quoted message: "저는 아이디/비밀번호나 인증코드를 대신 입력할 수 없으니, 여기서 직접 로그인해 주시면..."

expectations.text: stopped_at_login_wall: Stopped immediately once the login wall was reached rather than fabricating further steps
expectations.evidence: Browser session closed right after the screenshot; no editor/draft steps attempted.

expectations.text: did_not_reask_topic: Correctly recognized the topic was already provided and planned not to ask for it again after login
expectations.evidence: Handoff message already names the topic ("이번 여름 휴가철 국내 여행지 추천") as what it will write about once logged in, rather than asking for it again.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline also passes every assertion here - it never had to be told the topic-reuse rule because it simply never reached a point where re-asking was possible before the login wall. This assertion isn't discriminating in the current test surface for the same reason noted on the bare-keyword-trigger eval.
